RELIEF ORGANS
SEND PETITION

Failure To Secure
Japanese Permit
Causes Delay

Police action in assisting landlords in the Settlement to evict refugee squatters has again been postponed to enable relief organizations to find suitable premises for camp sites, announcement of the Shanghai Municipal Council yesterday stated.

The Council's decision came as a result of a joint petition made by several parent refugee relief organizations in which it was pointed out that eviction of some 25,000 people at the present time would seriously jeopardize public health and peace in the Settlement.

To Carry Out Court Orders

On lawful eviction for which a court order has been secured, the Council's announcement states:

"It is appreciated, however, that a legal obligation rests upon the Council to carry out evictions in individual cases where landlords have secured a court order lawfully authorizing an eviction."

The present postponement of the eviction of refugee squatters came as a result of the failure of the Shanghai International Red Cross to secure permits from the Japanese authorities to establish two camps in the extra-Settlement road areas.

Construction Stopped

Construction work on these projected camps was stopped by the Japanese early in June on the ground that no previous permission had been obtained for building of the camps. The International Red Cross originally planned to move some 25,000 refugees now occupying private properties to the new camps on the extra-Settlement roads by June 10.

The Council's announcement yesterday follows:

"A joint petition by the several parent refugee organizations has been submitted to the Council supplicating for a postponement of police action in assisting landlords in the eviction of refugees.

No Accommodation

"The petition represents that owing to delays in obtaining suitable camp sites, difficulties of procuring the necessary building materials and the protraction of negotiations aiming to secure the consent of all the authorities concerned, the refugee organizations have not yet found it possible to have ready alternative camps to accommodate the many thousand refugees whose eviction is sought by landlords. The difficulties represented by the refugee organizations have been investigated and found to be valid.

"The petition of the parent refugee organizations is supported by the Shanghai International Red Cross, which has stated that the compulsory eviction of several thousand refugees at the present time, when no alternative accommodation exists, would result in the peace of the city being jeopardized by consequent begging and stealing and forcible entry on the part of refugees. Health conditions would also be endangered by increasing the possibilities of infection through distribution of the refugees throughout the city.

To Allow Time

"It was the Council's hope that by a postponement in lending the assistance of its police to landlords in effecting evictions, sufficient time would be allowed the refugee organizations to provide alternative accommodation. These hopes, the Council regrets, have not materialized. The Council is compelled, therefore, in the interests of public peace, order and good health, further to withhold police action invoked by landlords to evict refugees. It is appreciated, however, that a legal obligation rests upon the Council to carry out evictions in individual cases where landlords have secured a court order lawfully authorizing an eviction.

"The Council is lending its assistance to the refugee organizations in their endeavors to expedite the provision of new camp accommodation for refugees."

难民驱逐行动
将予推迟

工部局暂缓
在此采取
警务行动

救济机构
递交请愿书

因未获日本方面许可
导致延误

上海公共租界工部局昨日宣布，为便于各救济机构为难民营寻找合适的处所，协助租界内房东驱逐难民非法占据者的警务行动再次推迟。

工部局作出此项决定，是基于几家主要难民救济机构联合提交的请愿书。请愿书指出，目前驱逐约25,000人将严重危及租界内的公共卫生与安宁。

执行法院命令

关于已获法院命令的合法驱逐行动，工部局公告声明：

“然而，工部局认识到，在房东已依法获得授权驱逐的法院命令的情况下，工部局负有在个别案件中执行驱逐的法律义务。”

此次推迟驱逐难民非法占据者，是由于上海国际红十字会未能从日本当局获得在越界筑路区域建立两个难民营的许可。

施工停止

日本方面于六月初以未事先获得建营许可为由，叫停了这些拟建难民营的施工工作。上海国际红十字会原计划于6月10日前，将目前占据私人房产的大约25,000名难民迁移至越界筑路区域的新难民营。

工部局昨日的公告全文如下：

“几家主要难民组织已向工部局提交联合请愿书，恳请推迟警方协助房东驱逐难民的行动。

无处安置

“请愿书称，由于获取合适营地选址的延误、采购必要建筑材料的困难，以及旨在获得所有相关当局同意的谈判旷日持久，难民组织尚未能准备好替代营地，以容纳房东要求驱逐的数千名难民。经调查，难民组织所述的困难属实。

“主要难民组织的请愿得到了上海国际红十字会的支持。该会表示，在目前没有替代住所的情况下，强制驱逐数千名难民，将导致难民随之乞讨、偷窃和强行闯入，从而危及城市安宁。此外，难民分散至全市各处会增加感染传播的可能性，从而危及健康状况。

给予时间

“工部局曾希望，通过推迟派出警察协助房东执行驱逐，能为难民组织提供足够的时间来提供替代住所。工部局遗憾地表示，这些希望并未实现。因此，为了公共和平、秩序和良好卫生的利益，工部局被迫进一步扣留房东所要求的驱逐难民的警务行动。然而，工部局认识到，在房东已依法获得授权驱逐的法院命令的情况下，工部局负有在个别案件中执行驱逐的法律义务。

“工部局正在协助难民组织，努力加快为难民提供新的营地住所。”

（批：8039 A/- 15 7 38）
（批：12/7）

驱逐难民行动

难民组织请愿书指出
尚未找到替代住所；
但承认房东权利

几家主要难民组织已向上海公共租界工部局提交联合请愿书，恳请推迟警方协助房东驱逐难民的行动。

请愿书称，由于获取合适营地选址的延误、采购必要建筑材料的困难，以及旨在获得所有相关当局同意的谈判旷日持久，难民组织尚未能准备好替代营地，以容纳房东要求驱逐的数千名难民。经调查，难民组织所述的困难属实。

主要难民组织的请愿得到了上海国际红十字会的支持。该会表示，在目前没有替代住所的情况下，强制驱逐数千名难民，将导致难民随之乞讨、偷窃和强行闯入，从而危及城市安宁。此外，难民分散至全市各处会增加感染传播的可能性，从而危及健康状况。

工部局感到失望

工部局曾希望，通过推迟派出警察协助房东执行驱逐，能为难民组织提供足够的时间来提供替代住所。工部局遗憾地表示，这些希望并未实现。

因此，为了公共和平、秩序和良好卫生的利益，工部局被迫进一步扣留房东所要求的驱逐难民的警务行动。然而，工部局认识到，在房东已依法获得授权驱逐的法院命令的情况下，工部局负有在个别案件中执行驱逐的法律义务。

工部局正在协助难民组织，努力加快为难民提供新的营地住所。

pages.en:
REFUGEE PROBLEM IN
SHANGHAI AREA

Although a great deal of sympathy must be extended to property owners whose premises have been invaded by refugees who refuse to move out, there will be general agreement, we think, with the decision of the Shanghai Municipal Council in withholding, for the time being, police co-operation in the matter of evictions. As the petition presented by several refugee organizations points out, the peace and good health of the city would be gravely jeopardized if there were the compulsory eviction of several thousands of refugees at a time when no alternative accommodation exists. The hopes of the Council that alternative accommodation would by now have been provided by the relief organizations have failed to materialize, and in this connection we understand that it is not on account of any unwillingness on the part of the organizations to undertake such a task but more because of the lack of sites within the foreign-controlled areas which could be used for this purpose. There is not the slightest doubt, however, that landlords have a clear legal right to the possession of their own property and that if they obtain a Court order a legal obligation rests upon the Council to carry out the terms of that order. What the Council is faced with is the preservation of public good order, and in desiring to maintain this it is adopting a festina lente policy which may be said to be for the benefit of the greater number and the greatest good.

Some further elucidation might help the general public to realize the extraordinarily difficult and tricky problem which this matter of refugees in illegal occupation of empty property constitutes. A figure as high as 30,000 has been mentioned by one relief organization, but, on the other hand, applications by landlords to the Council have been in respect of about 15,000 people. All landlords have not made complaints, so it might be taken for granted that the figure is certainly not less than 20,000. As to who these people are, it has been ascertained that fully eighty per cent. are women, children and either old or non-able-bodied men. They are practically all Shanghai people, for a recent census showed that something less than 3,000 farmer folk from the surrounding countryside are among the refugee population of Shanghai to-day. These are people whose country homes have been destroyed and who cannot get back on the land they normally till. More and more of the able-bodied refugees in Shanghai are finding work of one kind or another and great numbers of them are now living as squatters near to their places of employment. The people who ought legally to be evicted from the private property they now occupy are mostly those who have lost their breadwinners in the terrible upheaval of August, September, October and November of last year, and the vast majority of them are Shanghai folk in respect of whom it cannot be said that Shanghai has no obligations. In the early days of the vast refugee problem here quite large numbers were sent away to their own native districts and the majority of those who are now in refugee condition here are Shanghai's own for whom concern must obviously be shown.

A vast amount of splendid work has been done by voluntary refugee organizations and one has only to read the news bulletin of the Shanghai International Red Cross to realize what a tremendous debt the general communities of this city owe to those who have been doing such work for nearly a year past. But what needs to be understood is that part of this refugee problem looks like being of almost permanent character. The women, children and old men who have been rendered destitute and homeless cannot be passed on. Many of them can be taught how to earn something by way of simple handicrafts, but the question of their accommodation will have to be solved for them. The Council announces that it is lending its assistance to the relief organizations in their endeavours to expedite the provision of new camp accommodation for refugees, but the great difficulty about this is, as stated above, that within the Settlement boundaries there is nothing available. The possibilities of doing something further as regards Nantao are doubtless being explored, but the making available of a site or sites outside the Settlement boundaries is, perhaps, the most desirable piece of progress wanted to-day. Existing camps within the Settlement have no room for the refugees now occupying private property; there are no further sites available within the Settlement; landlords are rightly clamouring for the repossession of what is legally theirs; the majority of the refugees are Shanghai's own people who could not be sent away even if there were transportation facilities; and it is the making available of sites elsewhere near-by which is the most urgent need of the moment. These are the main ingredients in what will be recognized as an extremely difficult situation and one upon which the Council and all relief organizations are entitled to intelligent sympathy and co-operation. If we could get some of the present restrictions removed it would be a great gain, but certain people in Shanghai are doing the greatest disservice to this city by creating conditions under which it is impossible for any restrictions to be removed at all. Here is another angle on the futile and destructive terroristic activities of political agents, for it needs hardly to be stressed that Shanghai's refugee problem would quickly diminish if we could get on with work which lies to be done in the now closed areas.
pages.zh:
上海地区的难民问题

尽管对于那些房产被拒绝搬离的难民侵占的业主们必须给予极大的同情，但我们认为，公众普遍会赞同上海工部局暂时不在驱逐事宜上提供警务合作的决定。正如几家难民组织所提交的请愿书指出的那样，在没有任何替代住所的情况下，强制驱逐数千名难民将严重危及城市的安宁与公共卫生。工部局曾希望救济组织届时能提供替代住所，但这一希望未能实现；在此方面，我们了解到，这并非由于各组织不愿承担此项任务，而更多是因为在外人控制区域内缺乏可用于此目的的场地。然而，毫无疑问，房东对其自有财产拥有明确的合法占有权，且如果他们获得法院命令，工部局便负有执行该命令条款的法律义务。工部局面临的是维护公共良好秩序的问题，为了维持这一秩序，它采取了一种“欲速则不达”（festina lente）的政策，可以说这是为了大多数人的最大利益。

进一步阐明或许有助于公众认识到，难民非法占据空置房产这一事项构成了一个极其困难和棘手的问题。一家救济组织提到的数字高达30,000人，但另一方面，房东向工部局提出的申请涉及约15,000人。并非所有房东都提出了投诉，因此可以假定该数字肯定不少于20,000人。至于这些人是谁，经查明，整整百分之八十是妇女、儿童以及年老或无劳动能力的男子。他们实际上都是上海人，因为最近的一次人口普查显示，在当今上海的难民人口中，来自周边乡村的农民不到3,000人。这些人的乡村家园已被毁，无法回到他们通常耕种的土地上。上海越来越多的有劳动能力的难民正在找到各种工作，其中许多人现在作为非法占居者生活在靠近其工作地点的地方。依法应从其目前占据的私人房产中被驱逐的人，大多是在去年八月、九月、十月和十一月的可怕动荡中失去养家糊口者的人，其中绝大多数是上海本地人，对于这些人，不能说上海没有义务。在这个巨大的难民问题初期，相当多的人被送回了他们的原籍地区，而目前处于难民境况的大多数人是上海本地人，显然必须对他们表示关切。

志愿难民组织已经做了大量出色的工作，人们只需阅读《上海国际红十字会》的新闻简报，就能意识到本市各界社区对近一年来从事此类工作的人们欠下了多么巨大的债务。但需要理解的是，这部分难民问题看起来具有近乎永久性的特征。那些变得赤贫和无家可归的妇女、儿童和老人不能被转送走。许多人可以被教导如何通过简单的手工艺赚取一些收入，但必须为他们解决住宿问题。工部局宣布，它正在协助救济组织努力加快为难民提供新的营地住宿，但正如上述，这方面的巨大困难在于，在租界范围内没有任何可用之地。关于在南市采取进一步行动的可能性无疑正在探索中，但在租界范围之外提供一处或多处场地，或许是当今最需要的进展。租界内现有的营地没有空间容纳目前占据私人房产的难民；租界内没有更多的可用场地；房东正合理地强烈要求收回 legally 属于他们的财产；大多数难民是上海本地人，即使有运输工具也无法将他们送走；而在附近其他地方提供场地是当前最迫切的需求。这些是被公认为极其困难的局势中的主要因素，工部局和所有救济组织有权获得明智的同情与合作。如果我们能解除目前的一些限制，那将是一个巨大的收获，但上海的某些人通过制造使得任何限制都无法解除的条件，给这座城市带来了最大的损害。这是政治代理人徒劳且具破坏性的恐怖主义活动的另一个角度，因为无需强调，如果我们可以继续在现已封闭的区域进行有待完成的工作，上海的难民问题很快就会减少。

NEWLY-BORN REFUGEE BABIES

A new branch of the large-scale refugee work in Shanghai was opened recently at 110 Robison Road, where the Shanghai Refugee Maternity Centre is now located. Expectant mothers are received from the various camps all over the city. They come with their families and stay in sheds attached to the hospital. Later they are taken into the hospital and spend their post-natal hospitalization there. Picture shows the first eight babies to be born at the hospital.
[World News.

REFUGEE MATERNITY
CENTRE OPENED

Drive For $40,000 To Be
Launched On July 10;
Good Response Seen

In order to fight the high mortality rate among newly-born refugee babies and their mothers, the Shanghai Refugee Maternity Centre was opened early last month and is now in full operation at 110 Robison Road, a large number of babies having already seen the first light of day at the new hospital.

The Shanghai Refugee Maternity Centre, which is just another of the large-scale refugee relief organizations in Shanghai, has been organized by the Shanghai International Red Cross, the Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee, the Chinese Women's Clinic and other organizations.

Expectant mothers are taken in from the respective refugee camps, all over the city, sometime prior to the time that they expect their babies and are looked after, given medical attention, special nourishment, sunshine and fresh air and better living conditions, in matsheds attached to the Maternity Hospital itself. The expectant mothers are allowed to take along their families. This arrangement enables the doctors to better take care of the women. A clinic is also maintained at the centre, where the mothers and other members of their families are given free medical attention.

The hospital now has 100 beds for mothers during their post-natal hospitalization. The hospital is capable of increasing its capacity to 200 beds in case of necessity.

A drive for $40,000, the amount which is estimated will be necessary for the operation of the Centre for one year, will be launched on July 10, and a good response is expected.

新出生的难民婴儿

上海大规模难民工作的一个新分支最近在罗宾森路110号开设，上海难民营产妇中心现位于此处。来自全市各个营地的孕妇被接收。她们与家人一同前来，住在附属于医院的棚屋中。随后她们被接入医院，并在那里度过产后住院期。图片展示了在该医院出生的前八名婴儿。
[世界新闻。

难民营产妇中心
开幕

7月10日将发起募集4万美元活动；
预计反响良好

为了对抗新生难民婴儿及其母亲的高死亡率，上海难民营产妇中心于上月初开业，目前在罗宾森路110号全面运作，已有大量婴儿在这家新医院见到了第一缕阳光。

上海难民营产妇中心只是上海大型难民救济组织之一，由上海国际红十字会、上海紧急救济委员会、中国妇女诊所及其他组织组建。

孕妇在预产期前的一段时间从全市各自的难民营中被接收，并在附属于产妇医院本身的草棚中得到照顾，接受医疗护理、特殊营养、阳光和新鲜空气以及更好的生活条件。允许孕妇携带家人。这种安排使医生能够更好地照顾这些妇女。中心还设有一个诊所，母亲及其家庭的其他成员在此接受免费医疗护理。

医院目前设有100张床位，供母亲产后住院使用。如有必要，医院有能力将容量增加到200张床位。

预计中心运营一年所需的4万美元募捐活动将于7月10日启动，预计将获得良好的响应。

pages.en:
Refugee Maternal Centre Is
Opened For Relief Work

First Refugee Baby Is Named “Amos” In Honour
Of Dr. Amos Wong; Many Donations Received
From Individuals And Firms In Shanghai

The Shanghai Refugees Maternity Centre, a project jointly sponsored by a number of local organizations including the Shanghai International Red Cross, the International Relief Committee and the Salvation Army, received its first patients on Monday. At noon time that day the first refugee baby made his appearance. Reports state that as a tribute to the promotional efforts made by Dr. Amos Wong, the boy will be named Amos.

The Shanghai Refugees Maternity Centre is located at 110 Robison Road where a large residential building has just been repaired and cleaned for use as a maternity hospital, while on the adjacent lot, four mat-shed camps have been erected to house the relatives and children of the refugee-mothers.

The hospital has 100 beds, but eventually will be prepared to accommodate 200 patients. It has Dr. Beatie of the Seventh Day Adventist Mission as its superintendent, and Miss Follette of the same mission as chief of its nursing staff. Many of the medical equipments and appliance for the Centre are loaned by the Shanghai Sanitarium.

The project has been made possible chiefly through the generous support given by the Chinese Women’s Club of Shanghai. Several weeks ago, when the need for a maternity hospital for refugees was felt the Chinese Women’s Club donated a sum of $1,000 for the initial expenses. Subsequently, the Club agreed to pay for the budget of the Centre for the first month, amounting to $3,000.

Donations Promised

Donations supporting this maternity project have also been received from many individuals and local organizations such as the Y’s Men’s Club, the Amity Lodge, and the St. John’s University Christian Service League. More funds will be needed to finance this important relief project, and a campaign will soon be launched by the Committee of Management.

The Shanghai International Red Cross will provide basis food for the patients and the refugees at the Centre, besides giving a portion of the funds required for building the mat-sheds. Several local drug stores and firms have already promised to donated such useful articles as linen, cotton and soap.

It is learnt that of the 100,000 war refugees now confined in some 130 camps in Shanghai, no less than 33 per cent. are women. Thousands of these women are maternity cases, and need urgent medical attention. It is believed that the Shanghai Refugees Maternity Centre will now greatly relieve the local hospital situation.

The Centre is managed by a Committee composed of the following: Dr. J. E. Baker, ex-officio, Mrs. Y. Y. Tsu, chairman, Mrs. K. T. Kuo, secretary, Brigadier B. Morris, vice-chairman, Mr. John Wei, treasurer, Mrs. Ernest Tso, representing the Chinese Women’s Club, Mrs. J. R. Sun, National Y.W.C.A.; Miss T. Y. Zia, Shanghai Y.W.C.A.; Mrs. R. R. Johnson, Child Welfare Association, Mrs. A. L. Dawson, Amity Ladies Circle; Mr. K. Y. Li, the International Relief Committee; Mr. S. E. Chang, Shanghai Emergency Relief Society; Mr. N. B. Doodha and Mr. C. H. Lowe, the Shanghai International Red Cross; Mr. Lewis Mason, Shanghai Y’s Men’s Club; Dr. J. H. Jordon, S.M.C. Public Health Department; Dr. T. F. Huang, Chinese Medical Associations; Dr. L. Butka, Shanghai Sanitarium; and Mrs. Carrie Lu Lei, Public Health Service.

The daily report on refugee work in the international Settlement for June 6 is as follows: Camps under inspection by Public Health Department 128. Refugees therein 76,165.

难民产妇中心开启救济工作

首位难民婴儿为纪念黄安素博士取名“阿莫斯”；收到上海个人及商号的多笔捐款

上海难民产妇中心是由上海国际红十字会、国际救济委员会和救世军等多家本地机构联合赞助的项目，于周一接收了首批病人。当天中午，第一名难民婴儿降生。据报道，为表彰黄安素（Amos Wong）博士在推广该项目中所作的努力，这名男婴将被取名为阿莫斯（Amos）。

上海难民产妇中心位于罗宾森路（Robison Road）110号，那里的一栋大型住宅楼刚刚修缮并清理完毕，用作妇产医院；而在相邻的地块上，已搭建起四个草棚营地，用于安置难民母亲的亲属和子女。

医院设有100张床位，但最终将准备容纳200名患者。该院由基督复临安息日会传教团的比蒂（Beatie）博士担任院长，并由同一传教团的福莱特（Follette）小姐担任护理主管。中心的许多医疗设备和器具由上海疗养院（Shanghai Sanitarium）借出。

该项目的实现主要得益于上海中国妇女俱乐部的慷慨支持。几周前，当人们意识到难民营需要一家妇产医院时，中国妇女俱乐部捐赠了1,000美元作为启动资金。随后，该俱乐部同意支付中心第一个月的预算，金额为3,000美元。

承诺捐款

支持这一产妇项目的捐款也来自许多个人和本地组织，如青年会男士俱乐部（Y’s Men’s Club）、友济堂（Amity Lodge）和圣约翰大学基督教服务联盟。为资助这一重要的救济项目，还需要更多资金，管理委员会即将发起募捐活动。

上海国际红十字会将为中心的病人和难民提供基本食物，此外还拨付部分资金用于建造草棚。几家本地药店和商号已承诺捐赠亚麻布、棉花和肥皂等实用物品。

据悉，在目前被困于上海约130个营地的10万名战争难民中，女性占比不少于33%。这些妇女中有数千人处于待产状态，急需医疗关注。相信上海难民产妇中心现在将大大缓解本地医院的紧张状况。

该中心由一个委员会管理，成员如下：J. E. 贝克（J. E. Baker）博士（当然委员），徐永祚夫人（Mrs. Y. Y. Tsu，主席），郭德洁夫人（Mrs. K. T. Kuo，秘书），B. 莫里斯（B. Morris）准将（副主席），魏约翰（John Wei）先生（司库），曹尔尼斯特夫人（Mrs. Ernest Tso，代表中国妇女俱乐部），孙科夫人（Mrs. J. R. Sun，中华全国基督教女青年会）；夏廷瑛（T. Y. Zia）小姐，上海基督教女青年会；R. R. 约翰逊夫人（Mrs. R. R. Johnson，儿童福利协会）；A. L. 道森夫人（Mrs. A. L. Dawson，友济女士团契）；李国钦（K. Y. Li）先生，国际救济委员会；张寿镛（S. E. Chang）先生，上海急赈会；N. B. Doodha 先生和 C. H. Lowe 先生，上海国际红十字会；刘易斯·梅森（Lewis Mason）先生，上海青年会男士俱乐部；J. H. 乔登（J. H. Jordon）博士，工部局公共卫生处；黄廷芳（T. F. Huang）博士，中华医学会；L. 布特卡（L. Butka）博士，上海疗养院；以及陆雷 Carrie Lu Lei 夫人，公共卫生服务处。

6月6日公共租界难民工作报告如下：经公共卫生处检查的营地128个。其中难民人数76,165人。

New Maternity
Center Opened
For Refugees

Shanghai Relief Bodies
Co-operate On Aid
Project

The Shanghai Refugees Maternity Center, a project jointly sponsored by a number of local organizations including the Shanghai International Red Cross, the International Relief Committee and the Salvation Army, received its first patients on Monday. At noon that day the first refugee baby was born at the Center. As a tribute to the efforts made by Dr. Amos Wong in promoting the new enterprise the body will be named Amos.
The Shanghai Refugees Maternity Center is located at 110 Robison Road where a large residential building has just been repaired and cleaned for use as a maternity hospital, while on the adjacent lot, four mat-shed camps have been erected to house the relatives and children of the refugee-mothers.

Has 100 Beds

The hospital has 100 beds, but eventually will be prepared to accommodate 200 patients. It has Dr. Beatie of the Seventh Day Adventist Mission as its superintendent, and Miss Follette of the same mission as chief of its nursing staff. Many of the medical equipments and appliances for the Center are borrowed from the Shanghai Sanitarium.
The project has been made possible chiefly through the generous support given by the Chinese Women's Club of Shanghai. Several weeks ago, when the need for a maternity hospital for refugees was felt the Chinese Women's Club donated a sum of $1,000 for the initial expenses. Subsequently, the Club agreed to pay for the budget of the Center for the first month, amounting to $3,000.

Other Groups Contribute

Donations supporting this maternity project have also been received from many individuals and local organizations such as the Y's Men's Club, the Amity Lodge, and the St. John's University Christian Service League. More funds will be needed to finance this important relief project, and a campaign will soon be launched by the Committee of Management.
The Shanghai International Red Cross will provide basic food for the patients and the refugees at the Center, besides giving a portion of the funds required for building the mat-sheds. Several local drug stores and firms have already promised to donate such useful articles as linen, cotton and soap.
Of the 100,000 war refugees now confined in some 130 camps in Shanghai, no less than 33 per cent are women. Thousands of these women are expectant mothers, and need urgent medical attention. It is believed that the Shanghai Refugees Maternity Center will now greatly relieve the local hospital situation.
The Center is managed by a Committee composed of the following: Dr. J. E. Baker, ex-officio, Mrs. Y. Y. Tsu, chairman, Mrs. K. T. Kuo, secretary, Brigadier B. Morris, vice-chairman, Mr. John Wei, treasurer, Mrs. Ernest Tso, representing the Chinese Women's Club, Mrs. J. H. Sun, National Y.W.C.A.; Miss T. Y. Zia, Shanghai Y.W.C.A.; Mrs. R. R. Johnson, Child Welfare Association; Mrs. A. L. Dawson, Amity Ladies Circle; Mr. K. Y. Li, the International Relief Committee; Mr. S. H. Chang, Shanghai Emergency Relief Society; Mr. N. B. Doodha and Mr. C. H. Lowe, the Shanghai International Red Cross; Mr. Lewis Mason, Shanghai Y's Men's Club; Dr. J. H. Jordon, S.M.C. Public Health Department;

WATER IN REFUGEE CAMPS
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—May I use the columns of your paper to report some of my investigations into the water situation among refugees? In my letter entitled "A Cup of Cold Water," the plea was not meant to be taken literally as a plea for cold water. The term was used with the intention of reminding Christians of a certain Galilean's words as to a cup of cold water given in His name.

As we would expect, the Salvation Army has handled the problem of water for the refugees in their camp in a manner to command admiration. "Boiling water is to a Chinese what whisky is to a Scotsman," said Brigadier Morris. "Rice and boiling water are the two essentials for refugees. Given those two things, they will survive." There was no doubt that they were surviving! An we entered the gate, opposite to 555 Route De Sieyes (around the corner from the Community Church), at 8 a.m. yesterday morning, we met 900 healthy and moderately clean youngsters marching off to school. Proceeding to the boiling water stove, we saw a long line, each with his bucket. The size of the bucket made no difference, as the dipper used gave the same amount of water to each one. Three times a day this boiling water stove is going full blast, and the people get their ration of boiling water as they get their ration of rice. We might have left this camp joyously elated, but we did not. Here was a camp with spacious grounds, clean kitchen, splendid water arrangements, a matshed infirmary and clinic, ample living quarters, and only used to a little more than half of its capacity! Equipment that would care for 7,500, and only 4,500 in the camp! Lying close by was land that would accommodate 10,000 more. Memories of the pathetic plight of refugees who live in the street, or, worse still, who live in the dark, dank buildings on Shansi Road, and in other portions of the Central District, came to mind. "Why don't you bring those poor folk here?" we inquired. "Because the French Municipal Council decrees that no more refugees are to be allowed," was the reply. A Municipal Council has a duty to protect its people from a large influx of undesirables, but to the lay mind it is incomprehensible that an equipment already set up and going should be allowed to lie unused while tens of thousands rot in the dark buildings in the Central District! Surely, some adjustment should be worked out between the authorities of the two districts!

"Some of the old women in those Central District camps haven't seen the sun since last August," remarked the Brigadier. Perhaps some of the babies have never seen the sun, we thought. And here are wide open spaces, and sunshine, and food and water! Night in those buildings in the Central District must be a carnival time for rats and roaches. Water seems a matter of minor importance when sunlight and room to move about is denied, but even here it is a problem. A Red Cross visitor writes: "How do you think the people in one building get their water? From the waste pipe of a hotel, by removing a stone or so around the drain pipe!"

One of the first gifts to come in to the Red Cross marked especially for water was a gift of $200 from a lady. I was shown the camp to which this gift brought piped water. Seven shiny new taps were counted, and as we walked the length of the camp to count them, we saw a long rice line in the sun. They would be thirsty by the time they got their rice, we thought, and although the water was not yet turned on (May 31), it was to be turned on "to-day," the manager said. It was a comforting thought.

Another camp visited was opposite 311 Yu Yuen Road, behind Little Florist. A well-run camp, apparently; clean, accommodating 844 persons. By the kitchen stood the water wagon that brings water for cooking from the Fire Brigade. We were shown that pipes had been laid, and we were told that as they were outside the Settlement, it would take $400 or more to connect the water. "Meantime, what do the people do for drinking water?" The manager's face registered astonishment. "Why, they can go out and buy hot water. Over a hundred people in this camp have work." It is good to know they are so prosperous, but looking around at the children, we doubted that anyone had enough water to drink. The plight of mothers with small babies was one that stirred our sympathies.

The Red Cross has been hard at work making a survey of those camps without a supply of water. The Rev. A. E. Small, successor to Mr. Crawford, of the Red Cross Food and Shelter Committee, is attacking the problem with energy. We shall hope soon to have a report from him as to how the money contributed for this purpose is being used. To-day, we happen to know that he is working on the problem of getting water containers to camps that have nothing to put the water in if it is brought to them!

ALICE GREGG.
Shanghai, June 7, 1938.

难民营中的用水问题
致《字林西报》编辑：
先生，——我能否借用贵报版面，报告我对难民用水状况的一些调查？在我题为《一杯凉水》的信中，我的呼吁并非字面意义上要求提供凉水。使用这个词是为了提醒基督徒记住那位加利利人所说的话，即奉他的名给人一杯凉水。

正如我们所料，救世军在其营地处理难民用水问题的方式令人钦佩。“开水对中国人而言，就像威士忌对苏格兰人一样，”莫里斯准将说。“米饭和开水是难民的两大必需品。有了这两样东西，他们就能生存。”毫无疑问，他们确实活下来了！昨天早上8点，当我们进入位于西爱咸斯路（Route De Sieyes）555号对面（社区教堂拐角处）的大门时，我们遇到900名健康且较为整洁的少年正列队去上学。走到烧水炉旁，我们看到排着长队，每个人都提着桶。桶的大小无关紧要，因为使用的舀勺给每个人分配的水量相同。这个烧水炉每天三次全速运转，人们像领取配给米一样领取配给的开水。我们本可以欢欣鼓舞地离开这个营地，但我们没有。这是一个拥有宽敞场地、干净厨房、出色供水设施、草棚医务室和诊所、充足居住空间的营地，但仅使用了其容量的一半多一点！设备足以照顾7,500人，而营地中只有4,500人！附近还有可容纳另外10,000人的土地。我想起了那些流落街头，或者更糟的是，住在山西路及中区其他地段黑暗潮湿建筑物里的难民的悲惨境遇。“你们为什么不把那些可怜的人带到这里来？”我们问道。“因为法公董局规定不再允许接收更多难民，”这是回答。市政当局有责任保护其民众免受大量不受欢迎者的涌入，但在外行人看来，难以理解的是，已经建立并运行的设备竟被闲置，而数以万计的人却在中区的黑暗建筑中腐烂！显然，两个地区的当局之间应该达成某种调整！

“中区那些营地里的一些老妇人自去年八月以来就没见过太阳，”准将 remarked。也许有些婴儿从未见过太阳，我们心想。而这里有开阔的空间、阳光、食物和水！中区那些建筑物的夜晚一定是老鼠和蟑螂的狂欢时刻。当阳光和活动空间被剥夺时，水似乎成了次要问题，但即使在这里，水也是一个问题。一位红十字会访客写道：“你认为一栋楼里的人如何获取用水？通过移开排水管周围的一块或多块石头，从酒店的废水管取水！”

最早送给红十字会的指定用于供水的礼物之一，是一位女士捐赠的200美元。有人带我看了这笔捐款带来自来水的营地。数了数有七个闪亮的新水龙头，当我们走遍营地清点它们时，看到阳光下排着长长的领米队伍。我们想，等到他们领到米时肯定会口渴，虽然水还没有通（5月31日），但经理说“今天”就会通水。这让人稍感安慰。

参观的另一个营地位于愚园路311号对面，小花店后面。这显然是一个管理良好的营地；干净，容纳844人。厨房旁边停着从消防队运来烹饪用水的水车。有人向我们展示管道已经铺设好，并告诉我们，由于它们在租界之外，接通自来水需要400美元或更多。“与此同时，人们怎么解决饮用水？”经理脸上露出惊讶的神色。“哦，他们可以出去买热水。这个营地里有一百多人有工作。”得知他们如此富裕固然好，但环顾周围的孩子们，我们怀疑是否有足够的水喝。带着幼婴的母亲们的困境激起了我们的同情。

红十字会一直在努力调查那些没有供水的营地。红十字会食品与住所委员会克劳福德先生的继任者 A. E. 斯莫尔（A. E. Small）牧师正精力充沛地着手解决这一问题。我们希望很快能从他那里得到关于为此目的捐赠的资金如何使用情况的报告。今天，我们碰巧知道，他正在解决向那些即使送来水也没有容器盛放的营地提供储水容器的问题！

艾丽斯·格雷格（ALICE GREGG）
上海，1938年6月7日。

Terror Grips
Hankow City,
Says Refugee

Inhabitants Rarely Go
Out Into Streets In
Fear Of Air Raid

CHINA'S CAPITAL SAID
PANIC-STRICKEN

TOKYO, June 7.—Japanese
air raids have turned Hankow
into a panic-stricken city
whose inhabitants seldom ven-
ture into the streets and whose
population is only about one-
fifth of what it was before the
hostilities, according to a
Chinese woman refugee who
sought safety in Tsingtao.

Residents of Hankow started
evacuating in April, the woman
said, according to a press report of
an interview with her received by
the Foreign Office to-day.

The woman, whose name was
given as Li Lan-fang, said many im-
portant military buildings have been
destroyed by successive Japanese
air raids.

"Trying to get rewards, many
people were informing against each
other as spies," she said. "I was dis-
gusted with them. Chinese women
employees of the Government offices,
including typists, were discharged
on the ground that women are slaves
of vanity and spies.

"News of overwhelming victories
by Chinese soldiers were broadcast
often, but nobody knew whether
they were true.

"Living costs in Hankow were
very high. One box of matches cost
20 cents, three-cent tobacco cost 15
cents and 10-cent tooth powder cost
60 cents.

"Banks were paying back only a
small percentage of the money de-
positors wanted to withdraw every
day. Because of all these things
the people became frightened and
there was rioting. I parted from
my parents and brothers and went
to Tsingtao alone."—Domei.

193

难民称
汉口城陷入恐怖

居民因惧怕空袭
极少走上街头

据称中国首都
陷入恐慌

东京，6月7日电。——据一位在青岛寻求避难的中国女难民称，日本飞机的空袭已使汉口变成一座陷入恐慌的城市，居民很少冒险走上街头，人口仅约为战事爆发前的五分之一。

该女子称，据外交部今日收到的一份关于采访她的新闻报导，汉口居民于四月开始撤离。

这名女子名叫李兰芳（Li Lan-fang，音译），她说许多重要的军事建筑已在日军连续的空袭中被毁。

“许多人为了获取赏金，互相告发对方是间谍，”她说。“我对他们感到厌恶。政府机关的中国女性雇员，包括打字员，都以女性是虚荣的奴隶和间谍为由被解雇。

“经常广播中国军队取得压倒性胜利的消息，但无人知晓这些消息是否属实。

“汉口的生活费用非常高。一盒火柴售价20分，原本3分的烟草售价15分，原本10分的牙粉售价60分。

“银行每天只向储户支付其要求提取款项的一小部分。由于所有这些原因，人们变得惊恐不安，并发生了骚乱。我与父母兄弟分离，独自前往青岛。”——同盟社。

绝食者恢复进食；
必须于今日离开营地

上海最近的绝食者、福煦路白俄战争难民营食物的“良心拒服兵役者”菲加雷托（N. Nick Figaretto）和尤金·尔蒂谢夫（Eugene Rtischeff），昨晚仍在营地内，但奉令须于今日上午11时前离开。然而，这两人已结束绝食。

根据法国警察的命令，这两人原定于昨天上午11时前离开。但在时限到达之前，他们向警方抱怨未能找到住所，并请求额外宽限24小时。他们的请求获准，但被告知今天不再延期。警方称，要么他们自行离开，要么被驱逐出去。

除菲加雷托和尔蒂谢夫外，另一名难民尼古拉·戈洛涅茨（N. Golonetz，音译）也奉令离开营地。后者虽未参与绝食，但被指支持另外两人的“暴动”。《字林西报》昨晚获悉，这三名男子将每人每月获得15美元以资补助。只要他们仍属于失业人群，就将领取这笔钱。一旦找到工作，补助金即行停止。

菲加雷托于5月22日开始绝食，以抗议他声称的难民营管理部门在向难民分配每日口粮方面的违规行为。法国警察受邀进行调查，据悉他们发现一切正常，因此作出了驱逐“暴动者”的决定。

pages.en:
Refugees Occupying Private
Houses In Settlement Offer
Authorities Acute Problem

Fifty-Five Dwellings Commandeered By Destitute
Hordes Illegally; Landlords Press Police
For Restoration, But Alternatives Few

Since the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai last August, countless thousands of refugees have passed through the city, many of whom have remained within the limits of the port's two foreign-controlled areas.

Thousands were herded into camps, into vacant buildings and empty lots. Thousands roamed the streets. Still other thousands commandeered vacant houses, mostly Chinese-style dwellings, when towards the latter part of October, cold winds began to drive them off their temporary quarters in the nooks and crannies of the city's sidewalks.

Now these thousands, occupying approximately 55 private buildings in the International Settlement, constitute an acute problem for which neither relief organizations nor the police force has been able to formulate a practical solution.

Landlords Press Police

For months now proprietors of these buildings have been pressing the S. M. Police to evict the refugees, but recently it has become noticeable that the destitute hordes are becoming more and more impatient of restraint, and there is a fear that they might get out of control if any indication of force is to be shown in negotiations with them.

Since many of the occupants of these premises are receiving support from various relief committees, the latter have been approached by the police who requested assistance in finding new quarters for these refugees should they be evicted from the properties they now illegally occupy.

Of the landlords who seek the restoration of their property, only a small percentage is being compensated for the loss in potential rent by relief bodies. For the great majority, this "squatting" of refugees in their buildings is a total loss in revenue.

No Alternative

Police can not turn a deaf ear to the pleas of these landlords, which have recently changed to pressing demands. But there is no alternative but to let matters stand as they are for the time being. To evict the refugees would mean the turning loose of not only thousands of men, but also of thousands of women and children to the mercy of the elements. Also, it is against the policy of the S.M.P. to have thousands of hostile, destitute people roaming the streets of the Settlement—even if it were possible to evict the refugees by sheer force. It is felt by the police, and this belief is endorsed by relief bodies, that the refugees must stay where they are for another month at least.

Relief organizations are meanwhile negotiating with the landlords for a compromise. It is suggested that in return for the restoration of their buildings, proprietors grant relief organizations vacant lots upon which mat sheds may be built for the accommodation of the refugees. But even in the event of this compromise being reached, the plan can not be put into effect immediately, for to expose the refugees to the bitter below-zero weather of the present cold snap with no better protection than mat shed is not to be contemplated.

With the advent of warmer climes, it is felt, there is every possibility of the problem being amicably settled to the mutual satisfaction of both the landlords and refugees, both of whom must be equally considered.

There is but one other problem to be considered. That the refugees will move once offered other premises is regarded as a certainty, but to offer premises, mat sheds must be built, and funds for the erection of these are still lacking.

pages.zh:
难民占据公共租界
私人住宅给当局
带来严峻问题

五十五处住宅被贫困人群非法强占；房东向警方施压要求收回，但替代方案寥寥无几

自去年八月上海中日战事爆发以来，成千上万的难民流经本市，其中许多人留在了港口两个外国控制区的范围内。

数千人被赶入营地、空置建筑物和空地。数千人在街头游荡。还有数千人强占了空置房屋，大多是中式住宅，这是因为到了十月下旬，寒风开始将他们从城市人行道角落和缝隙中的临时栖身之所驱离。

如今，这些占据了国际公共租界内约55栋私人建筑的数千人，构成了一个严峻的问题，无论是救济组织还是警察部队都未能制定出切实可行的解决方案。

房东向警方施压

数月来，这些建筑的业主一直向工部局警务处（S. M. Police）施压，要求驱逐难民，但最近值得注意的是，这群贫困的人越来越不耐烦受到约束，人们担心如果在与他们谈判中表现出任何使用武力的迹象，局势可能会失控。

由于这些场所的许多居住者正接受各种救济委员会的资助，警方已联系后者，请求协助为这些难民寻找新的住处，以防他们被从现在非法占据的房产中驱逐。

在寻求收回房产的房东中，只有少数人从救济机构那里获得了潜在租金损失的补偿。对绝大多数人来说，难民在其建筑中的“非法占据”意味着收入的完全损失。

别无选择

警方不能对这些房东的恳求充耳不闻，这些恳求最近已转变为迫切的要求。但目前除了维持现状外，别无选择。驱逐难民不仅意味着将成千上万的男子，还将成千上万的妇女和儿童置于自然环境的摆布之下。此外，让成千上万充满敌意、贫困的人在租界的街道上流浪，也违背了工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的政策——即使有可能通过纯粹武力驱逐难民。警方认为，且这一观点得到救济机构的认可，难民必须至少在原地再停留一个月。

与此同时，救济组织正在与房东谈判以达成妥协。有人建议，作为收回建筑物的回报，业主应向救济组织提供空地，以便搭建草棚供难民居住。但即使达成这种妥协，计划也无法立即实施，因为在当前的寒潮中，气温降至零下，若让难民暴露在严寒中，仅以草棚作为庇护，这是不可考虑的。

人们认为，随着气候变暖，这个问题很有可能得到友好解决，使房东和难民双方都满意，这两方的利益都必须得到同等考虑。

还有一个问题需要考虑。一旦提供其他住所，难民将会搬走，这被视为必然，但要提供住所，就必须建造草棚，而建造这些草棚的资金仍然缺乏。

November 12, 1937.    4    Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE REFUGEES IN NANTAO

Throughout yesterday enemy planes carried out bombings in Nantao. In order to maintain order within their districts, the Police Authorities of the French Concession closed down the iron gates at the various intersections between the Concession and Chinese territory. The iron gates at the Old North Gate was left open for refugees to enter the Concession from Nantao, while residents who desired to go to Chinese territory were only allowed to pass through the gate at the corner of Rue Porte de l'Ouest and Boulevard de Montigny. This measure was adopted as a means to regulate communications. Consequently, Min Kuo Road, i.e. Boulevard des Deux Republiques, was fully congested with refugees.

At 3 p.m. yesterday, through the efforts of the responsible officials of the safety zone, the iron gates of the Foreign Cemetery along Boulevard des Deux Republiques, at the corner of Rue Pere Hue outside Kiu Mou Dee (九畝地), were left open and more than 2,000 refugees were admitted to the Cemetery pending other accommodation being prepared for them. About 500 refugees entered the Concession by jumping over the gate at Rue des Peres.

There are at present about 50,000 refugees being given accommodation in the safety zone in the northern part of Fang Pang Road. They have have already been without food for several tens of hours. For this reason, a meeting was held at 4 p.m. yesterday at the Y.M.C.A. by the Shanghai International Relief Association, at which it was resolved:-
(1) That Father Jacquinot of the International Relief Association be asked to request the French Concession Authorities to open as many iron gates as possible so as to facilitate the conveyance of foodstuffs for the relief of refugees.
(2) That the Shanghai Branch of the Relief Committee, the Pootung Fellow Countrymen's Association and the Federation of Charitable Associations undertake the accommodation of those refugees who have already been sent to the safety zone.
(3) That all food supplies contributed by the various charitable organizations be concentrated at the International Relief Association so as to facilitate their transportation.

According to Messrs. Tsai Yung-sung (蔡雲生) and Ho Tung-kung (胡冬根), members of the No. 7 Rescue Corps, there are at present more than 40,000 refugees confined in the safety zone in the City. They have been without any food for two days and several children have already died of hunger. Despite negotiations conducted by Mr. Loh Pah-hong (陸伯鴻) with the French Municipal Authorities for the opening of iron gates, no result has so far been reached. It is, therefore, to be sincerely hoped that local philanthropists and enthusiastic persons will devise immediate measures for the relief of these refugees and open negotiations with the French Concession authorities so as to save the refugees from starvation.

1937年11月12日。    4    晨间译文。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

南市难民

昨日全天，敌机在南市进行轰炸。为了维持其辖区内的秩序，法租界警察当局关闭了租界与中国领土之间各个路口的铁门。老北门的铁门保持开放，供难民从南市进入租界，而希望前往中国领土的居民仅允许通过西门路（Rue Porte de l'Ouest）与孟斗班路（Boulevard de Montigny）拐角处的城门。采取这一措施是为了管制交通。因此，民国路（即两共和国路，Boulevard des Deux Republiques）挤满了难民。

昨日下午3时，经安全区负责官员的努力，位于两共和国路、九畝地外神父路（Rue Pere Hue）拐角处的外国公墓铁门保持开放，2000多名难民被允许进入公墓，等待为他们准备其他住所。约500名难民翻越神父路（Rue des Peres）的铁门进入租界。

目前，约有5万名难民在方浜路北部安全区内得到安置。他们已有数十小时没有食物。为此，上海国际救济协会于昨日下午4时在青年会举行会议，决议如下：
(1) 请国际救济协会的饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）请求法租界当局尽可能多地开放铁门，以便运送救济难民的食品。
(2) 由救济委员会上海分会、浦东同乡会和慈善团体联合会负责安置已送往安全区的难民。
(3) 各慈善机构捐赠的所有食品集中到国际救济协会，以便于运输。

据第七救援队成员蔡雲生先生和胡冬根先生称，目前市区安全区内困有4万多名难民。他们已两天没有任何食物，几名儿童已饿死。尽管陆伯鸿先生已与法市政当局就开放铁门一事进行谈判，但迄今未取得结果。因此，真诚希望本地慈善家和热心人士制定紧急措施救济这些难民，并与法租界当局展开谈判，以使难民免于饥饿。

November 9, 1937.    4    Morning Translation.

THE NANTAO SAFETY ZONE

Mayor O.K. Yui of the Shanghai City Government issued on November 8 the following notification which appears in to-day's issue of the "Min Pao" and other local newspapers :-
"This City Government has been approached by the Shanghai International Relief Commission of the China Red Cross Society with a suggestion that a portion of Nantao bounded on the south by Fang Pang Road (方浜路) and on the east, west and north by Boulevard des Deux Republiques (Min Kuo Road) be demarcated as a zone for the temporary accommodation of refugees. This City Government has also been assured that this is entirely a measure for the relief of refugees; it will in no way menace the sovereign and administrative rights of this Government as the duty for the maintenance of peace and order within this safety zone will still be in the hands of the Chinese Police.
"As this arrangement is intended for the relief of refugees and was proposed out of humanitarian motives, the National Government was informed and permission has since been granted for the establishment of such a safety zone in Nantao, which will formally come into being as from noon November 9. Apart from notifying the various parties concerned, this notification is hereby published for the general information of the public."

This safety zone can accommodate some 100,000 refugees. Chinese Police will undertake the maintenance of peace and order and they will be authorized to carry pistols and batons. The Shanghai International Relief Commission will undertake the adjustment of food supplies to the refugees in this area. Red Cross flags will be hoisted at the four corners of this zone. It is understood that all public bodies located within this zone, such as the City Temple, the Small World Amusement Resort, schools and churches, will be converted into camps for the accommodation of refugees.

According to information secured by the Shun Shih News Agency, more than 10 red cross flags prepared by the International Relief Commission were hoisted at the various intersections on Fang Pang Road at 4 p.m. yesterday. These flags bear the name in both English and Chinese of the International Relief Commission so as to save the zone from bombing by Japanese planes. It is said that all the refugees who have escaped from Pootung during the past few days will be given accommodation within this zone.

According to information obtained by the Sin Sin News Agency, the Small World Amusement Resort, the Nan Yuan and Zung Hsiang Koo of the City Temple have been converted into refugee camps by the Relief Commission. The Shanghai Municipality Relief Branch Association has secured the use of the Pearl Dealers' Guild at Huh Ka Pang Road as a refugee camp, while the Shanghai Mohammedan Refugees Relief Association has established its 6th refugee camp on Huh Ka Road. It is learned that in all some 5,000 refugees were sent to this safety zone yesterday.

日期 15

1937年11月9日。上午4时译。

南市安全区

上海市政府市长俞鸿钧于11月8日发布如下通告，刊登于今日《民报》及其他本地报纸：——
“本市府接中国红十字会上海国际救济委员会建议，拟将南市一部分区域划为难民临时收容区，该区域南以方浜路为界，东、西、北三面以两共和国路（民国路）为界。本市府亦获保证，此纯属救济难民之措施，绝不损害本政府之主权及行政权，因维持该安全区内和平秩序之责仍由中国警察承担。
“鉴于此项安排旨在救济难民，且出于人道主义动机，已呈报国民政府并获准在南市设立此类安全区，自11月9日中午起正式成立。除通知各有关方面外，特此布告，以周知公众。”

该安全区可容纳约10万名难民。中国警察将负责维持和平与秩序，并被授权携带手枪和警棍。上海国际救济委员会将负责调整该地区难民的食物供应。该区四角将悬挂红十字旗。据悉，位于该区内的所有公共机构，如城隍庙、小世界游乐场、学校和教堂，都将改建为收容难民的营地。

据顺时新闻社获得的消息，昨日下午4时，国际救济委员会准备的十余面红十字旗已悬挂在方浜路的各个路口。这些旗帜上均用中英文标有国际救济委员会的名称，以使该区免受日本飞机轰炸。据说，过去几天从浦东逃出的所有难民都将被安置在该区内。

据新新新闻社获得的消息，小世界游乐场、城隍庙的南园和宗祠已被救济委员会改建为难民营。上海市救济分会协会已获准使用胡家浜路的珠业公所为难民营，而上海穆斯林难民救济协会已在胡家路建立了其第六难民营。据悉，昨天共有约5,000名难民被送往该安全区。

Extracts from Report on the 13th Meeting
of Shanghai Rice Price Fixing Committee

(Central Markets, Jan.9,1941)

(3) Complaint from Vay Zung Tah Rice Hong regarding
the recent arrest of one of its employees in the
Rice Market by the S.M. Police on the charge of
demanding higher prices than that fixed by the
Committee.

The case had subsequently been sentenced by the
Court to 10 months' imprisonment. The Chairman
remarked that according to the complainant, the whole
incident was a misunderstanding as the prices demanded
by the accused was actually the officially fixed
prices plus fees for transportation and therefore could
not be considered as a case of overcharging. Mr. C.K.
Woo, Chairman of the Rice Market Control Committee,
confirmed that the statement was true but added that
the accused's accounts would not appear misleading had
he separated the actual rice accounts from the
transportation charges instead of putting them
together. At the suggestion of Mr. H.P. Kang, it
was then decided that in future notice would be given
to the dealers to the above effect.

（中央市场，1941 年 1 月 9 日）

(3) 伟宗大（Vay Zung Tah）米行投诉，其一名雇员近期在米市被上海公共租界工部局警务处逮捕，指控其索要高于委员会规定价格的价格。

该案随后被法院判处 10 个月监禁。主席指出，据投诉人称，整个事件是一场误会，因为被告索要的价格实际上是官方定价加上运输费，因此不能视为哄抬物价案。米市管制委员会主席吴克刚（C.K. Woo）先生证实该陈述属实，但补充说，如果被告将实际米账与运输费分开列示，而不是混在一起，其账目就不会显得具有误导性。经康华平（H.P. Kang）先生建议，会议决定今后向经销商发出上述内容的通知。

REPORT

Subject...... Arrest of rice dealers for selling rice above the limit.

Made by...... D. S. I. Logan ........................................ Forwarded by ...... D. I. Crawford

At 10.45 a.m., May 9, Loh Pao Chu (陸宝初),
age 45, native of Paoshan, chief shop assistant of
Sung 生大 Dah Rice Shop, 414 Rue Tenant de la Tour,
and one Li 李華 Hwa, age 34, native of Kashing, rice
broker, residing at Lane 361, 4 East Seward Road,
were observed by C.D.C.199 to be engaged in a
dispute in the Rice Market, Tsing Lien Koh Teashop,
Foochow Road over the payment of a transaction in
the sale of rice. The former accused the latter
of having collected $10 in excess of the actual
price agreed upon between them. On being
questioned, Li Hwa made the following statement:-
On May 7, he purchased on behalf of
Loh Pao Chu, 15½ "zars" of Kan Mee rice from the
cyclists engaged in transporting rice from the
Shanghai suburbs, at Haining Road, at $45.80 per
"zar". The rice was delivered to the Sung Dah
Rice Shop, and the price, which totalled a figure
above $690.00 but less than $700.00 (the exact
amount he cannot remember but he knows that it
is recorded in an account book in the Sung Dah
Rice Shop) was paid by him to the cyclists
concerned after he had received same from one
Kan (甘) of the Sung Dah Rice Shop. In
addition he received for himself a commission
of $3.00.

（左侧手写批注）：
Hand them
both over to
the French
Police & report
any action
taken against
them.
The offence lies
in selling
6 jars at
$46 per jar
in the French
Concession.
Copy of this
report to
F. Police.

Rd.
5 / 9/25.
D. S. I. Logan
E. G.

报告

主题...... 逮捕以高于限价出售大米的米商。

制作人...... 副督察长 Logan ........................................ 转呈人 ...... 督察 Crawford

5月9日上午10时45分，陆宝初（Loh Pao Chu），45岁，宝山籍，福州路天潼路414号生大米行首席店员，以及李华（Li Hwa），34岁，嘉兴籍，米经纪人，住西华德路东4号361弄，被便衣警员199号观察到在福州路青莲阁茶馆米市场内因一笔大米交易的付款问题发生争执。前者指控后者收取的金额比双方商定的实际价格多出10美元。经讯问，李华作出如下陈述：-
5月7日，他代表陆宝初，在海宁路从从事从上海郊区运输大米的自行车夫手中购买了15½“扎”赣米，每“扎”45.80美元。大米被运送至生大米行，总价超过690.00美元但少于700.00美元（确切金额他不记得，但他知道记录在生大米行的账簿中），他在从生大米行的甘（Kan）姓人士处收到该款项后，支付给了相关的自行车夫。此外，他自己收取了3.00美元的佣金。

（左侧手写批注）：
将两人均移交给
法国警察局，并报告
对他们采取的任何
行动。
违法行为在于
在法租界内
以每扎46美元的价格
出售6扎大米。
本报告副本
送法国警察局。

阅。
9月25日 / 5
副督察长 Logan
